topics.title: Welcome to Magic Git
topics.summary: A native macOS Git client with six sidebar panels, File tabs, a session info card, and factory-default shortcuts.

sections.text: Magic Git is a native macOS Git client. It drives git, gh, and glab either on this Mac or on a remote POSIX host over SSH — an SSH session works on the host directly, with no local clone. A connected session has six sidebar panels — Repository, History, Branches, Stashes, Forge, and Worktrees — plus File tabs for more than one repository.
The sidebar session card
The bottom of the sidebar shows where you are and holds two buttons.

items: Repository — the repository name (the tab alias if you set one, otherwise the folder name). Hover for the full path. Ahead/behind counts and a dirty or conflict dot sit on the right; their tooltip reads, for example, "2 uncommitted · 1 ahead", or "Clean, in sync".
Location — This Mac for a local session, or the SSH host. Hover for user@host:port.
Workspaces — opens the Connections Manager (see Connections Manager).
Logout — ends the session after a Log out? confirmation. Nothing on the host is deleted.

sections.text: Help versus live shortcuts

This window (Help ▸ Support & Help, ⌘?) is the user guide. It lists factory-default shortcuts. Your remaps are in Keyboard Shortcuts (⌘/) and Settings → Keyboard Mappings. The Troubleshooting category covers connection, forge, refresh, and access problems.

sections.title: App Sandbox Security
sections.text: Local repository access uses macOS security-scoped bookmarks, so later launches reopen a folder without asking again.

topics.title: Connecting to Repositories
topics.summary: Open a repository on this Mac or on an SSH host from the Connections Manager or Recent Repositories.

sections.text: The landing screen offers the Connections Manager and Recent Repositories. Recent Repositories lists the last 5 repositories you opened; it reads No Recent Repositories until you open one.
Add an existing repository
In the Connections Manager, Add existing repository opens the Add Existing Repository sheet.

items: Location — Local (this Mac), this SSH session ("<host> (this session)", shown only for an unsaved session), or one of your saved connections.
Folder — Choose… shows the macOS folder picker for a local location; Browse… shows a folder browser on the host.
Save repository — remembers it in the Connections list, with an optional Label.
Enable filesystem monitor (faster status on large repos) — turns on git fsmonitor for this repository.
Scoped work-tree repo (dotfiles) — for a bare or separate-git-dir repository. It is detected automatically from the folder; see Connections Manager.
Open — opens the repository in a tab.

sections.text: A local repository gets a security-scoped bookmark, so later launches reopen it without asking. Opening a linked worktree first asks you to Grant access to the main repository.
Connect to an SSH host
Add connection (the + in the Connections Manager, or New SSH connection when it is empty) opens Add SSH Remote.

items: Host, Port, and Username — the SSH server and the account to sign in as.
Password, or Private key (PEM) — sign in with a password, or Load private key… or paste the key. Key passphrase is only needed for an encrypted key.
Repository path — required: the absolute path of the repository to open after connecting.
Scoped work-tree repo (dotfiles) and Git directory — for a repository whose git data lives elsewhere (GIT_DIR); the Repository path becomes its work tree.
GitLab token and GitHub token — optional personal access tokens that sign glab or gh in on the host.
Save connection — keeps the profile, with secrets in secure storage, under an optional Label.

sections.text: Connect opens the repository. An unsaved connection still works for the session and appears in the Connections Manager as "(unsaved)".

sections.title: Automatic Reconnection
sections.text: If SSH drops mid-session, a Connection interrupted overlay retries with an attempt counter and elapsed timer. Stop Retrying pauses auto-reconnect and shows Connection lost (Reconnect or Start Fresh). Cancel fully disconnects and confirms if the session is at risk.

topics.title: Connections Manager
topics.summary: Saved local repositories and SSH connections: open, edit, remove, and scope them.

sections.text: The Workspaces button in the sidebar (or Connections Manager on the landing screen) opens your local repositories and saved SSH hosts. Its toolbar has Saved workspaces, Add connection, Add existing repository, Clone repository, and Create repository.
Sections

items: Local Repositories — repositories on this Mac.
Remote Repositories — each saved SSH connection. Click a host to expand its repositories; the row shows how many ("N repos").
An unsaved session appears as "<name> (unsaved)" and is read-only here.
A worktree chip marks a linked worktree you granted access to.
When nothing is saved: Add local repository, New SSH connection, Clone repository, and Create repository.

sections.text: Editing entries

items: Edit connection — change the Label, Host, Port, Username, password, key, passphrase, or tokens. A secret field left blank keeps the stored one ("Leave blank to keep current").
Delete connection — deletes the connection and its stored credentials, after a confirmation.
Edit repository (remote) — Label, Path on the host (repoints the entry), and Git directory for a scoped repository, plus the fsmonitor toggle.
Edit repository (local) — Label and fsmonitor. The Folder is fixed by its access grant; remove the entry and add it again to use a different folder.
Remove repository — removes the entry from the list. Files are not deleted.
The fsmonitor icon on a row toggles git fsmonitor ("Git fsmonitor off (click to enable)").

sections.text: Scoped and dotfiles repositories

A scoped work-tree repository keeps its git data outside the work tree — for example a dotfiles repo with GIT_DIR at ~/.home.git and your home folder as the work tree. Add Existing Repository detects this automatically. For SSH, tick Scoped work-tree repo (dotfiles) and fill in Git directory. Every git command then runs with that git directory. The filesystem monitor is unavailable for a scoped repository; it watches only tracked files instead.
The remote folder browser

Browse… opens Choose a folder on the connected host. Type an absolute path or move up with Parent folder. Toggle dotfiles with the eye button ("Hiding dotfiles (click to show)"), then press Choose This Folder.
Location and names

items: One glyph means the same thing everywhere — tabs, the context bar, the Location row, and Manager rows: a globe is an SSH host, a folder is this Mac.

One name is used everywhere for a repository: its tab alias if you set one, otherwise its folder name. The window title shown in Mission Control, the app switcher, and the Window menu reads "name (branch) — Magic Git".

topics.title: Clone and Create Repositories
topics.summary: Clone from GitHub, GitLab, or a URL, or create a new repository, on this Mac or an SSH host.

sections.text: Clone repository and Create repository are on the Connections Manager toolbar and under app: in the command palette. Both are step-by-step sheets with Back, Continue, and a final Clone or Create.
Clone

items: Target — This Mac, a saved connection, or this session (an unsaved SSH session).

Source — GitHub or GitLab browses the repositories your signed-in account owns (Forge host, Reload, Filter…); URL takes any address git clone accepts, HTTPS or SSH. An organization's repository you do not own needs URL.

Location — Folder name (prefilled from the source), then the Parent folder on this Mac (Choose…) or Parent folder on the host (Browse…). Options: Create parent folders if missing, Enable git fsmonitor, and Save to Local Repositories with a Label.
Review — check the summary, then Clone. Progress streams live. A failed or cancelled clone deletes the partial folder it created.

sections.text: Create

items: Target — This Mac, a saved connection, or this session.
Source — New folder (created inside a parent folder) or Existing folder (becomes the repository in place).

Remote — None, GitHub, GitLab, or Custom URL. GitHub and GitLab create the project with gh or glab (signed in on the target), with Visibility (Private or Public), Forge host, and Project description. Custom URL points origin at an existing remote. Replace existing origin remote (if any) applies to an existing folder.

Details — Repository name, Initial branch, and Git identity: the git identity (name and email) for this repository, prefilled from Settings and written into this repository only. For a new folder, Add a README (creates the initial commit); for an existing one, Commit all existing contents.

Namespace (optional) — for GitHub or GitLab, the owner or group to create under. Search namespaces… filters the list: Recently active (namespaces you used or opened repositories in, with when) first, then All you can create in. Leave it empty to create under your own account. You can also type a namespace that is not listed.
Review — check the summary, then Create. If a later step fails, the repository is kept and the failing step is reported.

sections.text: Where the result opens

The new repository opens in its own tab, or switches to a tab already open on it. It opens in the current tab only when it is a local repository you chose not to save ("Opens in this tab (not saved to Local Repositories)"), or when the target is the current unsaved session. With all 8 tabs open, clone and create are refused until you close one.

topics.title: File Tabs and Saved Workspaces
topics.summary: Open several repositories at once, rename tabs, save a set, and confirm before leaving risky work.

sections.text: File tabs are repository sessions, not the six sidebar panels. File ▸ New Tab (⌘T) or the + button opens another session; the + is disabled at 8 tabs ("Maximum of 8 tabs open"). Close Tab is on the File menu (disabled with one tab open) and on each tab's close button — ⌘W closes a viewer window, not a tab. The strip hides when only one tab is open.

items: Middle-click a tab to close it; drag a tab to reorder.
Each tab shows the location glyph (globe for SSH, folder for this Mac) and the repository name.
An orange dot means uncommitted changes. A red dot means conflicts.

sections.text: Saved Workspaces

Saved Workspaces (Connections toolbar, or Manage Saved Workspaces in the palette) saves the open set of saved repositories — each tab's alias and layout preset, plus which tab was active — and restores it later. Open reports any repository that failed without closing the ones that opened. Delete removes the saved set; open tabs are not affected.

items: Rename active tab (the pencil) opens Rename Tab and sets an alias for the active tab only. Leave it blank to clear the alias.
Only saved repositories can have aliases.

sections.text: Leaving a session

items: Close tab, Log out, Disconnect, and closing the window confirm only when work is at risk — uncommitted changes, or a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert still in progress.
Quit always asks "Are you sure you want to quit?". When a repository has work at risk, the dialog title becomes "Some repositories have active items pending…".

topics.title: Context Bar, Size, and Menus
topics.summary: The bar above every panel: navigation, repository status, view options, and the sync group.

sections.text: The workspace is compact below 720 px (navigator or canvas, not both; the sync group collapses; a Toggle sidebar button sits on the bar), standard from 720 to 1199, and wide at 1200 px and above.
Context bar, left to right

items: Back and Forward — move between places you visited in this repository.
Repository identity — name, branch, and status summary. On SSH it also shows the connection. Below 720 px the detail moves into a hover tooltip (Repository details).
View options — the workspace view options menu (below).
Activity — live operations (see Dashboard, Recovery, and Activity).
Stash changes and Refresh.
Fetch · Pull · Push · Sync — the sync group, last.

sections.text: The change-detection dot

Beside the repository name, a dot shows how Magic Git notices file changes: green means a live file watcher, orange means it is polling instead (slower; see Troubleshooting ▸ Refresh), and grey means nothing is watching — press ⌘R to refresh.
The sync group

items: Every verb that applies right now is highlighted: Fetch always, Pull when you are behind, Push when you are ahead, Sync when both.
The recommended verb carries the ↓N ↑M ahead/behind badge. Below 720 px only the recommended verb keeps a button.
More sync actions, beside the group, holds Pull with Rebase, Pull with Merge, Push and Set Upstream, Push Tags, Force Push with Lease, and Force Push.
Hover a dimmed verb to see why it is unavailable — for example "This branch has no upstream yet".

sections.text: View options

items: Show secondary action labels (off by default).
Show or hide Back, Forward, Sync actions, Stash, Refresh, Activity, View options, Status summary, and Connection status.
Commit in Focused sheet (default) or Commit in Task dock — where Commit… and ⌘G open the composer. Switching keeps your draft.
Presets Review, Commit, Investigate, and Minimal. Default is Review. Investigate names an inspector slot that is unused — Focus Inspector does nothing.

sections.text: Menus

File, Repository, Branch, Stash, Forge, and Worktree sit in the macOS menu bar with App, Edit, View, Window, and Help. Unavailable items stay visible and dim. View ▸ Focus Navigator, Canvas, Task Dock, and Activity exist and are unbound. Choosing a command from another panel switches there and runs it. Menus and Factory-Default Shortcuts lists every menu item.

topics.title: File View and Output
topics.summary: The docked file tree (⇧⌘E) and the live command Output log (⇧⌘O).

sections.text: File View is View ▸ Show File View (⇧⌘E). The workspace's left pane — the commit list, branch tree or stash list — is View ▸ Show Navigator (⌥⌘N); collapsed (as the Minimal preset leaves it), it shows a narrow rail at the left edge naming the pane, and clicking the rail brings it back. It is on by default but hidden until the canvas is at least 1200 px wide unless you Pin file view open. Hide and Collapse all sit on the Files header. There is no Changes | Files switch — the change list stays in the navigator and the tree is this third pane.
Output

Output (View ▸ Show Output View, ⇧⌘O) is a docked command log below every page — on Repository, below the changes list, beside the File view — visible by default. It shows git and SSH invocations, stdout, stderr, and exit codes, including doctor install output.

items: Fetch, pull, push, sync, Fetch & Prune, and clone stream their progress live as they run.
A Pull shows two commands: the fetch, then the merge or rebase.
After a pull, push, or sync, Output lists the files that were pulled or pushed.
Clear output empties the log; Hide output view closes it. Drag the top edge to resize.
The log keeps the last 2000 lines.

topics.title: Dashboard, Recovery, and Activity
topics.summary: Session health, reflog and snapshot recovery, and the live operations list.

sections.text: Dashboard
View ▸ Show Dashboard View (⇧⌘D) is a live overview of the session. It is not the Forge panel.

items: Connection — backend, host, reconnects, and the last drop.
Authentication — whether git, gh, and glab are installed and signed in, on this Mac and on the connected host.
Link latency (SSH keepalive) — one sample every 15 s.
Repository — upstream state, for example "This branch has no upstream".
Commit activity (30 days) with top authors, and Contributions (last 200 commits) as a heatmap.
Commands (this session) — command counts.
Change watcher — Live, Polling fallback, or Stopped.
Repository footprint — Measure runs git count-objects and suggests `git gc` when it would help.

sections.text: Recovery

View ▸ Show Recovery View (⇧⌘U) lists every place HEAD has pointed (the reflog) and the snapshots in refs/magic-git/snapshots/. A snapshot is taken automatically before each discard or delete and kept for 7 days. Use Recovery for state that Undo Git Operation can no longer reach.

items: Select a reflog entry, then Restore…: Checkout this state, Create branch here…, Reset current branch here (soft), Reset current branch here (hard), or Copy hash.
Select a snapshot, then Actions: Restore files, Delete snapshot, or Copy hash.

sections.text: Activity

Activity is on the context bar. Its icon spins while operations run; its tooltip counts them ("2 active operations", or failed ones). It opens a list of repository operations — Queued, Running, Completed, Failed, or Canceled — each with a live elapsed time.

items: Output reveals the command in the Output log.
Undo undoes the newest undoable operation.
Recovery opens the Recovery sheet.
While fetch, pull, or push runs, the Dock icon shows a progress bar; a clone shows its percentage.

topics.title: Settings
topics.summary: Timeouts, identity, sync defaults, opening files, auto-fetch, appearance, known hosts, shortcuts.

sections.text: Open Settings from Magic Git ▸ Settings… (⌘,) or the command palette. Changes apply after Save. Keyboard Mappings, Forget Host and Open files with save immediately.

items: Command timeouts — Network (fetch/pull/push) is a stall budget of 3 minutes by default: a fetch, pull, or push that prints no output for that long is stopped, while a slow transfer that keeps printing may run up to 30 minutes. Commit is a wall-clock limit of 5 minutes by default — raise it if a slow hook is cut off. The minimum for either is 5 seconds.
Committer identity — applied to every commit. Leave blank to use the repository's own git config. Magic Git always records unsigned commits (--no-gpg-sign).
Default sync behavior — Pull / Sync uses Fast-forward only, Rebase, or Merge (default Fast-forward only). Push tags by default is off.

Opening files — Open files with chooses the application Open file uses (Choose… or Reset). Left as System default, a file opens in whatever macOS opens that kind of file with. Open in Terminal always uses Terminal.app.
Background auto-fetch — Auto-fetch is Off, or every 5, 10, 15, or 30 minutes. Default is every 5 minutes.
Workspace appearance — Density Compact or Comfortable (default Comfortable), High contrast, and Reduce Motion, which follows macOS.
Known Hosts — Forget a recorded SSH host key.
Keyboard Mappings — Customize remaps. The live cheat sheet is ⌘/.
External tools — override binary paths and Scan the host (see Tool Health).

topics.title: Repository
topics.summary: Review, stage, and resolve changes in the Repository sidebar panel.

sections.text: The Repository panel (⌘1) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. The change list is Conflicts, Staged, Changes, and Untracked, with filter chips, Hide reviewed, and group-by status or directory. Review selected and Review all visible open multi-file review. A clean tree shows "Working tree clean".
Staging and diffs

items: Space toggles staging for the selected file or files. ⌘-click and ⇧-click select several.

Line staging works on unified, whitespace-exact diffs with blame off: select lines, then Stage, Unstage, or Discard Selection. Split and ignore-whitespace diffs are read-only. Per-hunk buttons also exist.
Drag unstaged files onto the staging banner to Stage; drag staged files to Unstage.

Right-click a change for Stage, Unstage, Discard Changes, Discard Staged Changes, Add to .gitignore, Delete Untracked File, Blame, Copy Relative Path, Copy Path, Reveal in Finder (this Mac only), and Open file.

sections.text: The commit bar

When the tree has changes, a bar under the list shows "N staged files · branch" with Unstage All, Stage All, and Commit… (⌘G). Committing — the focused sheet or the task dock, and Amend Last Commit… — is covered in Committing.
Conflicts

items: A conflicted file offers Use Ours (HEAD), Use Theirs (incoming), and Mark Resolved. During a rebase git swaps the roles, so the buttons read Use Onto (ours) and Use Commit (theirs).
Right-click offers Resolve Using … and Mark Resolved for several files at once.

While a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert is in progress, a banner reads "<Verb> in progress — resolve conflicts, then continue, or abort." with Continue and Abort <Verb> (for example Abort Merge). The same banner appears in Branches.

sections.title: No default shortcut
sections.text: Pull with Rebase, Pull with Merge, Push and Set Upstream, Push Tags, Force Push (no lease), Unstage All, and Abort Pending Operation have no default shortcut. Find them on the Repository menu, in the command palette, in the context bar's More sync actions, on the commit bar (Unstage All), and on the pending banner (Abort).

topics.title: Committing
topics.summary: Write and commit a message in the focused sheet or the task dock, optionally pushing too.

sections.text: Stage what you want, then press Commit… on the commit bar or ⌘G. By default this opens the Focused sheet over the workspace. To compose in a panel docked below the changes instead, choose Commit in Task dock in the context bar's View options. Switching keeps your draft.
The composer

items: The header reads "Commit N files" on the current branch. There is one message field.
Accept commits (⌘↩). Accept + Push commits, then pushes (⇧⌘↩).

Assistance (or Hide Assistance) offers Use a recent subject… (Load recent), Load template or Use template, a message policy advisory, and co-authors: enter a Co-author name and email, then Add co-author.
Regenerate appears when the staged files changed after the draft was generated ("Staged changes changed; review this draft or regenerate.").
A message produced by a prepare-commit-msg hook is marked "Generated by prepare-commit-msg. Review, Edit, or Accept."
Clear empties the message. In the task dock, Collapse hides the composer.
Escape closes the sheet and keeps your draft — except during the moment the commit itself runs.

sections.text: Commit and push

items: The sheet closes as soon as the local commit lands. With Accept + Push, the push continues in the background ("Committed. Pushing… you can close this; it continues in the background."), streaming into Output and listed in Activity.
If that push fails, an error dialog explains why, Activity marks the push Failed, and your commit stays in the local branch — push again once the problem is fixed.
Accept without push starts a quiet background fetch so ahead/behind counts stay current.

sections.text: Amending and signing

items: There is no amend checkbox. Use Repository ▸ Amend Last Commit… (unbound) for the working tree, or Amend last commit on the HEAD commit in History.
Commits are unsigned (--no-gpg-sign). If the repository enables commit.gpgsign, the composer says so.
Settings ▸ Committer identity sets the name and email for every commit.

topics.title: Fetch, Pull, Push, and Sync
topics.summary: What each sync verb runs, how progress is shown, and the guardrails before a risky push.

sections.text: The sync group on the context bar, the Repository menu, the palette, and the shortcuts all run the same commands. Progress streams live into Output; the Dock icon shows a progress bar and Activity lists the operation.
What each verb runs

items: Fetch — git fetch --prune on all remotes, without submodules.

Pull — a fetch of the upstream, then a merge or rebase against @{upstream}. The mode comes from Settings ▸ Default sync behavior: Fast-forward only (the default, never creates a merge commit), Rebase, or Merge. Pull with Rebase and Pull with Merge override it once.
Push — pushes the current branch, plus reachable annotated tags (--follow-tags) when Settings ▸ Push tags by default is on. Push and Set Upstream publishes a branch that has no upstream.
Sync — pull, then push.

sections.text: Guardrails

items: Pushing while the remote has commits you do not have asks "Remote has new commits": Pull, then Push; Push anyway; or Cancel.
Force Push with Lease and Force Push ask for confirmation first ("Force push"). With lease refuses if someone else pushed since your last fetch; Force Push overwrites unconditionally.
A pull is not recorded in the undo journal — use Recovery to go back.

sections.text: While a sync runs

items: Staging stays usable during fetch and push. Pull and Sync lock staging until they finish.

Hover a dimmed verb for the reason: "This branch has no upstream yet", "No remote is configured", "A fetch or push is already running", "Repository is disconnected", or "Another repository operation is running".

sections.text: Background fetching
Settings ▸ Auto-fetch (default every 5 minutes) fetches the default remote in the background so ahead/behind counts and remote branches stay current.

topics.title: History
topics.summary: Commit graph, filters, commit actions, interactive rebase, and the History window.

sections.text: The History panel (⌘2) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. It draws a topological commit graph with ref chips and a minimap — click the minimap to jump there. The context-bar primary is Refresh. Move the selection with ↑/↓ or J/K; Shift extends it; Esc clears it.
The filter bar

items: ⌘F focuses the filter. Plain words match the message. Terms: author:, file: (or path:), sha: (or commit:), after: (or since:), and before: (or until:). A bare commit hash of 5+ characters finds that commit; * and ? are wildcards; quote values with spaces, like author:"Jane Developer".
Filter by author, date, or path (the slider icon) opens a row with Author name or email, After date, Before date (dates like "2 weeks ago" work), a file-or-folder limit, and the Hide merges checkbox.
The footer counts matches ("First N matching commits — scroll for more") and offers Clear filters.
The All Branches icon (tooltip Show all branches) switches between HEAD and every branch. It has no keyboard shortcut — ⇧⌘B is Checkout Selected Commit, which asks for confirmation.
Recovery (reflog & snapshots) and Open History in new window are icons on the same bar.

sections.text: Commit actions

items: Single commit: Checkout, Branch from…, Branch from… in a new worktree…, Tag…, Cherry-pick, Revert, Interactive rebase from here…, Reset to the commit (soft / mixed / hard — hard asks first, because it overwrites all uncommitted changes), Amend last commit (HEAD only), and Copy SHA.

Two commits: compare them ("Comparing X → Y", Copy both SHAs). Several: cherry-pick or revert N, or copy N SHAs. Bulk cherry-pick and revert are disabled when the selection contains a merge commit — act on it alone to choose its mainline parent.
The diff header above a commit has word wrap, Copy full SHA, Open diff in a larger window, and a menu with the same commit actions.
Drop a branch onto a commit to merge it into the current branch (normal, no-ff, or squash), rebase the current branch onto it, or move that branch here.

sections.text: Interactive rebase

Interactive rebase from here… opens the Interactive rebase sheet. Set each commit to Pick, Squash, Fixup, or Drop; drag a commit to reorder it, or drop it onto another to squash them. Reword is unavailable because the rebase runs without an editor. It is disabled on the root commit.
Branch history and the History window

items: Branches ▸ Advanced ▸ Open reachable history shows a "History of <branch>" banner with Clear.
Open History in New Window (⇧⌘H) pops a live native History window.

topics.title: Branches
topics.summary: Browse and review local and remote branches and tags; merge, delete, tag, and publish.

sections.text: The Branches panel (⌘3) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. It is master–detail with two modes, Browse (branches, remotes, and tags) and Review (local branches compared with a base). The context-bar primary is Fetch & Prune (no default shortcut). With nothing selected, the detail pane shows branch statistics. Out-of-sync branches and how to fix them are covered in Branch Sync and Recovery.
Branch operations

items: ⌘B opens the New branch sheet (Name and Start at, defaulting to the selected ref or HEAD). After Create, choose Here or New worktree.
Double-click or press Enter to check a branch out. You can also check out in a new worktree.
⇧⌘M merges the selected branch into the current branch after a confirmation.
Delete (⌘⌫) always confirms. An unmerged branch asks again with Force Delete. A branch checked out in a worktree offers Remove Worktree and Delete.

Rebase the current branch onto another by dragging that branch onto HEAD ("Combine with …"), or use Reconcile… when it has diverged from its upstream. There is no general Rebase item on the context menu.
Right-click (or the detail pane's Advanced menu) for merge variants, Set upstream…, Unset upstream, Rename…, Pin to top, Copy name, and Delete branch.
Pin to top keeps a branch first. The folder icon switches between a flat list and grouping by folder.

sections.text: Review mode

items: Compared with picks the base (Recommended, Local, Remotes, Tags); Reset saved base returns to the default.
Sort: Smart, Activity, Name, Ahead, or Behind. Filter: Unpublished, Upstream gone, In a worktree, Has a request, No request, Failing CI, Mine.
Select several branches (⌘-click, ⇧-click, ⇧-arrow, or Space) and the detail pane becomes "N branches selected" with Pin, Unpin, Hide, and Delete if merged…. Batch actions never include Merge.
Hidden branches disappear from the list. The eye icon shows them again; then Unhide on a row.
With nothing selected, Review adds Merged and Conflicts filter chips and Scan for conflicts.
The detail pane compares the branch with the base: Overview, Changes, and Commits, with a Readiness prediction of a local merge (needs git 2.38+).
Branches with no commit in 3 months collapse into a stale group you can show or hide.

sections.text: Tags and remote branches

items: Create Tag (⇧⌘T) opens Create Tag: tick Annotated tag to add a Tag message, and Push to <remote> after creating.
Tags only on this machine are marked local only; one that points elsewhere on the remote is marked differs from <remote>. Push tag, or push all local-only tags from the section header.
Deleting a tag that also exists on the remote asks: Delete Local Only, or Delete Local and on the remote.
A remote branch offers Check out tracking branch and Delete branch on the remote.

sections.title: The Branch menu
sections.text: Publish, Create Pull or Merge Request, Compare with Base, and Open CI are on the Branch menu and the detail pane, with no default shortcut. Keyboard: Home, End, Page Up/Down, type to find, and ⇧F10 opens the context menu.

topics.title: Branch Sync and Recovery
topics.summary: What Not published, Diverged, and gone mean, and the guided actions that fix each.

sections.text: Branches explains why a branch cannot simply pull or push, and offers a named action for each case. Rows show a short chip; the detail pane explains the state and holds the action.
Not published
The branch has no upstream yet — it exists only here. The detail pane says so and offers Publish Branch, which pushes it and sets the upstream (the same as Push and Set Upstream).
Diverged
The branch and its upstream each have commits the other lacks ("N commits here, M there"). On the current branch, Reconcile… (row menu or Advanced) opens Reconcile with <upstream>:

items: Merge "<upstream>" into "<branch>" — the primary choice; keeps both histories.
Rebase "<branch>" onto "<upstream>" — replays your commits on top.
Reset "<branch>" to "<upstream>" — discards the commits that exist only here. It asks first (Reset to <upstream>?) and is reversible with ⌘Z or the undo toast.

sections.text: No common history

If the branch and its upstream share no common history, the detail pane says so and offers Merge (allow unrelated histories)…. A Merge unrelated histories confirmation warns that combining two independent histories may produce many conflicts; Merge Anyway runs git merge --allow-unrelated-histories.
gone
A gone marker means the upstream branch was deleted on the remote (merged or removed), so the local branch is likely stale. Confirm where its work landed before deleting it.
Cleaning up after Fetch & Prune

When Fetch & Prune finds local branches whose remote branch no longer exists, it asks Clean up stale branches? and lists them; Delete removes them locally. Branches that are not fully merged — for example squash- or rebase-merged ones — get a second Force Delete prompt.
Set upstream

Set upstream… (row menu or Advanced) sets the remote-tracking branch that pull, push, and the ahead/behind badges follow. It refuses a remote branch that does not exist yet: "If this branch has never been pushed, use Publish instead."
An operation in progress

While a merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert is paused on conflicts, a full-width banner across Branches reads "<Verb> in progress — resolve conflicts, then continue, or abort." with Continue and Abort <Verb>. Resolve the files in Repository, then Continue.
The Advanced menu

The detail pane's Advanced menu matches the row menu: Check out, Switch to its worktree, Check out in a new worktree…, Create Pull or Merge Request, Open on Forge, Open reachable history, Merge into current, Merge (no fast-forward), Merge (fast-forward only), Squash merge, Reconcile…, Set upstream…, Unset upstream, Rename…, Pin to top, Copy name, and Delete branch.

sections.title: Undo and Recovery
sections.text: Reconcile's Reset is recorded in the undo journal (⌘Z). A merge or rebase can be backed out with Abort while it is in progress, or afterwards from Recovery (⇧⌘U).

topics.title: Stashes
topics.summary: Shelve work with include-untracked, then apply, pop, drop, or branch from a stash.

sections.text: The Stashes panel (⌘4) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. Each card shows stash@{n}, the branch it came from, and its age. Filter stashes matches the subject, branch, or hash. Select a stash to preview its patch.
Creating a stash

Stash Changes (context bar, the panel's primary action, or ⇧⌘S) immediately runs git stash push --include-untracked with no prompt. Untracked files are always included. To set a message, use Stash ▸ Stash with Message… or Stash with message… in the panel's header menu.
Applying and removing

items: Apply (⌥⌘A) restores the stash and leaves it on the stack. Pop (⌥⌘P) restores and removes it. The row menu also offers Apply, restoring staged files and Pop, restoring staged files (--index).
Each card has inline buttons: Apply stash (keep in list), Pop stash (apply & remove), and Drop stash.
Drop (⌘⌫) deletes the selected stash after confirmation; it is recorded first, so ⌘Z undoes it.
Create branch from stash… is on the row menu.
The header menu (and the Stash menu) has Apply latest stash, Pop latest stash, and Clear all stashes…

topics.title: Forge
topics.summary: GitHub and GitLab in one panel: the Inbox, Browse sections, and closed or merged requests.

sections.text: The Forge panel (⌘5) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. It talks to GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab, on the host the repository lives on. The context-bar primary is New Pull Request or New Merge Request (New Request, disabled, while the forge is still being detected). Requests, reviews, merging, and issues are covered in Pull Requests, Merge Requests, and Issues; CI is covered in CI Runs and Pipelines.
Inbox and Browse

items: Switch between Inbox and Browse. Inbox is the default, and your choice is remembered.

Inbox collects open pull or merge requests, CI runs or pipelines that failed or are still running, and open issues. Chips filter All / PRs or MRs / CI / Issues. No blockers is a separate toggle that combines with them.
Pin to top or Snooze an Inbox row; pinned and snoozed rows gather under Pinned and Snoozed. Pinning and snoozing cancel each other and are remembered per repository.

Browse sections are Issues, PRs or MRs, Labels (view only), Milestones, Releases, and Workflow Runs or Pipelines. Every section can collapse, and stays collapsed. One Filter field filters every section. The + on the Issues header (also Forge ▸ New Issue… and the palette) starts a new issue.

sections.text: Open, closed, and merged

items: Request lists start with open items. Show closed pull requests (GitHub) or Show closed merge requests (GitLab) widens the list to closed and merged ones; the detail pane's State line tells them apart.
A closed request or issue can be reopened with Reopen. A merged request cannot.
Long lists stop at 50 with a Show N more row. Issues, CI, labels, milestones, and releases have their own Show all rows.

sections.text: A request's detail pane

items: The merge readiness strip shows blockers, or Ready to merge, Checking mergeability… (with Retry), or an auto-merge note.
Check out checks out the head branch (asking first if your tree is dirty).
Update branch (GitHub) or Rebase onto target (GitLab) appears as a button when the branch is behind its target.
Enable auto-merge or Cancel auto-merge sits on the action bar; Cancel Auto-merge is also on the Forge menu.
Approve (⌥⌘A), Merge (⇧⌘M), and Re-run Failed Jobs or Retry Pipeline (⌥⌘R) follow the detected host.

sections.title: Which host?
sections.text: Magic Git detects GitHub or GitLab from the origin remote, including self-hosted GitLab. If the repository has no remote, or the remote is not a recognized GitHub or GitLab host, the panel says so. See Troubleshooting ▸ Forge for sign-in and rate-limit messages.

topics.title: Pull Requests, Merge Requests, and Issues
topics.summary: Create, review, merge, and manage requests and issues from the Forge panel.

sections.text: Creating

items: New Pull Request (⌘N, the context bar, or the Forge menu) opens a form in the detail pane: Head branch, Base branch, Title, Description, Reviewers (comma-separated), Assignees (comma-separated), labels, a Milestone, and Create as draft. Preview changes shows the diff. Create pushes the branch with its upstream first.
New Merge Request is the same on GitLab, with Source and Target branches plus Mark as draft, Squash commits when merged, and Remove source branch when merged.
New issue — the + on the Issues section, the palette, or Forge ▸ New Issue… (no default shortcut). It takes a Title, Description, Assignees, labels, and a Milestone.
Dragging a local branch onto Forge opens the create form with that branch filled in.
Leaving a form with unsaved text asks Discard draft? (Keep Editing or Discard Draft). A draft survives switching panels.

sections.text: Rows and the right-click menu

items: Rows show a DRAFT badge, the CI state, review chips (approved, changes requested, review needed — only review needed on GitLab), and label chips.

Right-click a request for Open in browser, Copy link, Copy #N (GitHub) or Copy !N (GitLab), Check out branch, Comment…, Approve, Request changes… (GitHub only), Mark ready for review or Convert to draft, Edit…, the merge methods, and Close or Reopen.
Merge methods: GitHub offers Merge, Squash and merge, and Rebase and merge; GitLab offers Merge and Squash and merge, as the project allows. Drafts cannot be merged until marked ready.
Close asks first ("You can reopen it later."). Reopen does not.

sections.text: Merging

Merge opens a sheet after re-checking readiness: Merge method (the methods the project allows), Delete source branch after merge, and an optional commit Title and Body. The merge is pinned to the head commit shown in the summary, so a late push cannot slip in. The primary Merge button uses the project's default method; its menu offers the others.
Reviewing and editing

items: The detail pane lists Head/Base (or Source/Target), Author, State, Review, Merge status, Head SHA, Auto-merge, Labels, and Assignees, then the description, checks, and Comments (the last 50; open the forge for the full thread).
The More menu holds Comment…, Request changes… (GitHub only; a comment is required), Mark ready for review or Convert to draft, Edit… (Title and Description), and Close or Reopen.

sections.text: Issues

items: Right-click an issue for Open in browser, Copy link, Copy #N, Start work (GitHub only), Comment…, Assign to me (GitHub only), Edit…, and Close or Reopen.
Start work creates a branch for the issue and checks it out (gh issue develop).
The issue detail pane shows State, Author, labels, the description, and Comments, with Start work, Comment, Close or Reopen, and More (Edit…, Assign to me).
The Issues header shows a count such as "30 of 974"; Show all issues loads the rest.

topics.title: CI Runs and Pipelines
topics.summary: Workflow runs (GitHub) and pipelines (GitLab): jobs, logs, and re-running.

sections.text: Browse ▸ Workflow Runs (GitHub) or Pipelines (GitLab) lists the newest 10; Show all workflow runs or Show all pipelines loads more. Failed and running ones also appear in the Inbox. A request's detail pane shows its own checks.
Jobs and logs

items: Select a run or pipeline to see its Jobs, with Refresh jobs. Select a job to view its log in a resizable pane.
GitLab streams a running job's log live, and refreshes the job list every 5 seconds while jobs run. Scroll up and a Jump to latest button appears. Very long logs keep the last 256 KB.
GitHub updates job statuses live, but a job's log appears only after it finishes: "This job is still running. Logs are available once it completes."
GitLab merge-request pipelines are labelled "MR !N" or "MR !N (merged results)".

sections.text: Re-running

items: GitHub: Re-run failed jobs (⌥⌘R, the row icon, or Forge ▸ Re-run Failed Jobs) re-runs only the jobs that failed.
GitLab: Retry pipeline (⌥⌘R, the row icon, or Forge ▸ Retry Pipeline).

topics.title: Worktrees
topics.summary: Parallel checkouts in a nested strip — Overview plus Changes, History, Branches, and Stashes.

sections.text: The Worktrees panel (⌘6) is a sidebar page, not a File tab. Opening a worktree adds a checkout tab on the Worktrees strip (Overview | that checkout). That nested strip is not the File-tab switcher. Each checkout tab has Changes, History, Branches, and Stashes, and a Close tab button. Forge stays on the repository, not the checkout.
Overview

items: Every worktree is listed with chips for its branch (or "(detached abc1234)"), missing, locked (with the reason), main worktree, and open. A row shows at most two chips plus +N.
With only the main worktree, Overview shows No worktrees yet with Add Worktree….
A missing worktree offers Repair — I moved this folder and Prune — forget all missing worktrees….
The strip's menu has Prune stale worktrees and Repair all worktree links.

sections.text: Row menu

items: Open Worktree, and Open in Window — a separate Status window for that worktree (see Secondary Windows).
Reveal in Finder and Open in Terminal (this Mac only; Terminal.app), Copy Path.
Lock / Unlock, Move… (not while locked or missing), Repair… (when missing).
Remove Worktree…, and Remove Worktree and Delete Branch… (not for a detached HEAD). Removing one with uncommitted changes or a lock asks again (Remove Anyway).

sections.text: The Worktree menu (all unbound) offers Add, Open, Lock, Unlock, Move, Repair, Repair All, Prune, and Remove.
Adding a worktree

Add Worktree can create a new branch, use an existing one, or detach at a revision (Based on). Choose where it goes (Create in, with Choose…, and Folder name) — it must be outside the repository. Optional: copy ignored files such as .env*, and run a post-create command (remembered for next time; its output appears in Output). Open it when done opens the new worktree right away.
A local add records a security-scoped bookmark. SSH has no sandbox bookmark. A worktree created in the terminal prompts once on first open (Grant access to this worktree).

topics.title: File Viewer and Remote Edit
topics.summary: Floating viewer windows with Source and Preview, find, wrap, and editing files on an SSH host.

sections.text: View file opens a floating viewer window over the workspace, not the docked File View pane. Viewer windows can be dragged and resized, cascade when you open several, and reopen at the last size. Escape or ⌘W closes the front viewer.

items: Markdown, HTML, and SVG files open in Preview; switch to Source with the title-bar toggle. Links in a Markdown preview open in the browser.
The title bar also has Copy file contents, Word wrap, and Maximize (or double-click the title bar).
⌘F opens the find bar.
Binary files and files too large to display offer Open in Default App instead.

sections.text: Open file
Open file (on the change list and the file tree) opens the file in the application chosen in Settings ▸ Open files with — System default unless you pick one.
Editing a file on an SSH host

On an SSH session, Open file copies the file to a temporary folder on this Mac, opens it in that application, and uploads it back each time you save. If the file changed on the host in the meantime, Remote Edit Conflict asks before replacing it (Overwrite Remote).

topics.title: Diffs, Blame, and File History
topics.summary: Diff controls, multi-file review, blame, follow-renames history, image diffs, and LFS pointers.

sections.text: Diff controls

items: The diff header has Previous changed file and Next changed file, and Use split diff / Use unified diff. Its menu has Ignore whitespace (or Show whitespace changes), Expand context (or Use normal context), Show blame (or Hide blame), and Open diff in larger window.
Hunk and line actions need the unified, whitespace-exact diff. The diff mode is remembered per repository.

sections.text: Multi-file review

Review selected and Review all visible (Repository panel) step through files with Previous, Next, and Mark Reviewed. Bulk buttons act on every file in the review: Stage, Unstage, Discard, Delete, Ignore, and for conflicts Use Ours (HEAD), Use Theirs (incoming), and Mark Resolved.
Blame and file history

items: The blame gutter is off by default. Show blame on the diff, or open the Blame sheet ("Blame · path") from the change list or the file tree.
File history (git log --follow) is on the file tree, not the Changes list.
The file tree can View file, Open file, Mark Resolved, act on the staged or unstaged halves, Add to .gitignore, Blame, or Delete File (undoable).

sections.text: Images and LFS

items: Image diffs have three modes: Side by Side, Overlay (the new image at 50% over the old), and Slider (drag a divider). Each side shows its size in pixels and bytes. If the images cannot be compared, the diff falls back to a binary notice with Open in Default App.
Git LFS pointers are named as pointers — run git lfs pull on the host. They are not shown as a binary image.

topics.title: Drag and Drop
topics.summary: Stage, stash, cherry-pick, merge, rebase, branch, and create worktrees by dragging.

items: Unstaged files onto the staging banner = Stage; staged files = Unstage.
Dragging a selected row carries the whole selection.
Files onto Stashes = a stash of just those paths (include-untracked).
A stash card onto Repository = Apply (keep in list) or Pop (apply & remove).
A commit onto Repository = cherry-pick (confirm).
A commit onto Branches = New branch from that commit, checked out.
A commit onto History = Show it in History. A branch onto History = Show history of that branch.
A local branch onto Forge = create a pull or merge request (opens the form with the branch filled in).
A commit or branch onto Worktrees = the Add Worktree sheet.
A branch onto a History commit = merge, rebase, or move that branch here.
A commit onto a branch row = cherry-pick onto that branch; a branch onto HEAD = merge or rebase.
Esc cancels a drag.

topics.title: Secondary Windows
topics.summary: The native History window, detached Status windows, and the in-window diff pop-out.

items: The native History window is a singleton (⇧⌘H, View ▸ Open History in New Window, the History filter bar, or the palette).

A detached Status window shows the full Repository view for one path. Open one from Worktrees ▸ Open in Window; it is titled "Status — <repository> (<connection>)" and works for linked worktrees too. It shows Waiting for session… until the main window's session is ready, and a reconnecting banner if the connection drops.
The diff pop-out (Open diff in larger window) is an in-window float, not a native window.
While one of the native secondary windows is key, its View and repository menu key equivalents are stripped so they do not steal keys from that window. Menu clicks still act on the main session.

topics.title: Command Palette
topics.summary: Search go, git, forge, and app commands, plus branches, commits, files, stashes, and worktrees.

sections.text: Press ⌘K to open the command palette. Prefix with go:, git:, forge:, app:, branch:, commit:, file:, stash:, or worktree:. file: lists changed paths only, not the whole tree. Open Settings is a command — the palette does not search Settings keys.

items: go: switches panels, and lists Switch to tab <name> for each File tab and Open workspace <name> for each saved workspace.
git: includes Recovery: Browse Reflog & Snapshots.
forge: lists commands for the detected host only, plus Create Pull or Merge Request and Open CI.
app: holds Clone Repository, Create Repository, Manage Saved Workspaces, and Manage Connections.

sections.text: Commit-message and viewer actions are intentionally absent from the palette catalog.

topics.title: Menus and Factory-Default Shortcuts
topics.summary: Every factory-default shortcut, plus menu-only verbs. Remaps live under ⌘/.

sections.text: This topic catalogs every factory-default shortcut. Help ▸ Support & Help is ⌘?. Keyboard Shortcuts (the live cheat sheet of your remaps) is ⌘/. Settings → Keyboard Mappings saves remaps immediately.
Menus

File, Repository, Branch, Stash, Forge, and Worktree hold every toolbar verb. Some chords are shared across scopes (⇧⌘M, ⌥⌘A, ⌘N, ⇧⌘↩, ⌘⌫) — only the active panel's handler runs. Forge items act on the detected host: GitHub items for a GitHub repository, GitLab items for a GitLab one.

items: File — New Tab, Close Tab.

Repository — Fetch; Pull ▸ Pull, Pull with Rebase, Pull with Merge; Push ▸ Push, Push and Set Upstream, Push Tags, Force Push with Lease, Force Push; Sync; Stage All; Unstage All; Commit…; Amend Last Commit…; Stash Changes; Abort Pending Operation….
Branch — New Branch…, New Tag…, Publish Branch, Create Pull or Merge Request, Compare with Base, Open CI, Merge into Current Branch, Delete Branch….
Stash — Stash with Message…, Apply Stash, Pop Stash, Drop Stash…, Apply Latest Stash, Pop Latest Stash, Clear All Stashes….
Forge — New Issue…, New Pull Request…, New Merge Request…, Approve, Approve Merge Request, Merge Pull Request…, Merge Merge Request…, Cancel Auto-merge, Re-run Failed Jobs, Retry Pipeline.
Worktree — Add Worktree…, Open Worktree, Lock Worktree, Unlock Worktree, Move Worktree…, Repair Worktree, Repair All Worktree Links, Prune Stale Worktrees, Remove Worktree….

View — Show Output View, Toggle Sidebar, Show File View, Show Navigator, Show Dashboard View, Show Recovery View, Open History in New Window, Refresh, Command Palette, Focus Navigator, Focus Canvas, Focus Inspector (unused), Focus Task Dock, Focus Activity.
Help — Support & Help.

sections.text: No default shortcut

Use the menu or palette, and bind them in Keyboard Mappings if you want a chord: Toggle Sidebar, Close Tab, Focus Navigator / Canvas / Task Dock / Activity, Pull with Rebase or Merge, Push and Set Upstream, Push Tags, Force Push (no lease), Unstage All, Amend Last Commit… (working tree), Abort Pending, Publish, Create Pull or Merge Request, Open CI, Compare with Base, Stash with Message, Apply/Pop latest, Clear all, every Worktree verb, New Issue, Cancel auto-merge. Focus Inspector exists on the View menu and is unbound; the inspector slot is unused.

topics.title: Local and SSH Sessions
topics.summary: The same UI for a local Mac and a remote host; silent TOFU; Host Key Changed on mismatch.

sections.text: Local repositories use Process.start on this Mac. Remote repositories use the same screens over SSH. Both PEM (with passphrase) and password auth work, as do custom ports.
Host keys

The first time Magic Git sees a host it records the key silently (TOFU). If a known host presents a different fingerprint, a Host Key Changed dialog offers Cancel Connection or Refresh Key and Continue. Settings ▸ Known Hosts can Forget a recorded key.

topics.title: Undo, Redo, and Recovery
topics.summary: ⌘Z undoes the last git operation. Staging is not undoable. Redo is tags only.

sections.text: ⌘Z undoes the last git operation. A toast lasts about five seconds and pauses while you hover; click it to undo. The journal covers commit, amend, reset, checkout, create or delete branch or tag, stash drop/pop/clear/branch, discard, remove files, and hard-reset-shaped merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or revert. Unlike discard, staging is not undoable, and neither is a pull.

items: ⇧⌘Z redo applies only to atomic tag create or delete.
An empty journal toasts Nothing to undo or Nothing to redo.
If files changed after the operation, undo asks first (Files Changed Since → Overwrite).
If the repository moved on in a way the undo cannot safely reverse, the entry is discarded with an explanation.
Edit ▸ Undo is still text undo in a field.
Recovery (⇧⌘U) reaches reflog and snapshots that ⌘Z cannot.

topics.title: Tool Health
topics.summary: Check git, gh, glab, and file watchers on the host, and install what is missing.

sections.text: Tool health runs on a live connection, not the landing page. A banner appears when something is wrong: missing essential binaries are errors, and missing feature binaries or outdated versions are warnings. It offers Scan environment and Dismiss. Settings ▸ External tools has Scan and opens the same doctor.

items: Required — git 2.24 or newer, for every repository operation.
Feature — gh 2.0 or newer for GitHub, and glab for GitLab.
Optional — fswatch on macOS hosts and inotifywait on Linux hosts give live refresh; without them Magic Git polls. Linux hosts are not blamed for a missing fswatch.

sections.text: Environment health

The doctor sheet, Environment health, lists each tool as OK, Update, Not installed, or Override, with Re-check. Install with … runs a one-click install when it is safe (its output appears in Output); Copy command gives you the command to run yourself. With no network on the host, Install from file… — or drag a binary or .tar.gz onto the sheet — uploads and installs it (sideload).

topics.title: Output Log
topics.summary: The docked log of git and SSH invocations, stdout, stderr, and exit codes.

sections.text: Output (⇧⌘O) is the docked command log described in File View and Output. Recovery is a separate sheet — see Dashboard, Recovery, and Activity, and Undo, Redo, and Recovery.

topics.title: Connection Problems
topics.summary: Dropped SSH sessions, a changed host key, and missing tools on the host.

sections.text: The session dropped

Symptom: a Connection interrupted overlay with "Reconnecting… (attempt N)" and "Disconnected for …". Cause: the network or the SSH server went away. Fix: wait — it retries on its own. Stop Retrying pauses it and shows Connection lost, with Reconnect or Start Fresh. Cancel disconnects fully, and asks first if work is at risk.
Host Key Changed

Symptom: a Host Key Changed dialog showing the Previously trusted and Now presented fingerprints. Cause: the server's key differs from the one recorded the first time you connected — expected after a server rebuild, suspicious otherwise. Fix: if you did not expect a change, choose Cancel Connection and check with the server's owner. Otherwise choose Refresh Key and Continue. Settings ▸ Known Hosts can Forget a recorded key.
A command times out

Symptom: a fetch, pull, or push stops with a timeout. Cause: it printed nothing for the network stall budget (3 minutes by default). Fix: raise Network (fetch/pull/push) in Settings ▸ Command timeouts. A slow hook that cuts a commit off needs a larger Commit timeout.
A tool is missing or too old

Symptom: a red or orange Tool Health banner after connecting. Cause: git, gh, or glab is missing or older than Magic Git needs on that host. Fix: Scan environment, then install from Environment health — see Tool Health.

topics.title: Forge Problems
topics.summary: Sign-in failures, rate limits, repositories with no forge, and self-hosted GitLab.

sections.text: A sign-in problem

Symptom: "This looks like a sign-in problem — run `gh auth login` (or `glab auth login`) on the target, then refresh." with Open Dashboard. Cause: the forge CLI on the host running git is not signed in, or its token expired. Fix: run the auth login command on that machine — this Mac or the SSH host — or add a GitHub token or GitLab token to the saved connection. Dashboard ▸ Authentication shows which CLIs are signed in where.
Rate limited
Symptom: "… was rate limited by the forge. Try again in …". Cause: the forge is throttling requests. Fix: wait for the time shown, then refresh. Magic Git never retries on its own.
No remote detected, or Unsupported forge

Symptom: the Forge panel says No remote detected, or Unsupported forge. Cause: the repository has no remote, or its origin is not a GitHub or GitLab host Magic Git can recognize. Fix: add an origin remote that points at GitHub or GitLab. For a host whose name does not say which forge it is, sign gh or glab in to it — Magic Git asks the CLIs which hosts they are signed in to.
GitLab reports no project
Symptom: "GitLab reports no project at …". Cause: the origin path is wrong, or the token cannot see the project — GitLab answers both the same way. Fix: check the origin URL and the token's access.

sections.title: Self-hosted GitLab
sections.text: Every glab call is pinned to the host in the origin remote, so a self-hosted GitLab works even when glab's default host is gitlab.com. Sign glab in to that host (glab auth login --hostname <host>) on the machine that runs git.

topics.title: Refresh and Change Detection
topics.summary: Why changes appear late, what the orange dot means, and how to speed up status.

sections.text: Changes appear late

Symptom: the dot beside the repository name is orange, the Repository panel says "Polling for changes (watcher unavailable)", and Dashboard ▸ Change watcher shows Polling fallback. Cause: no live file watcher could start on the host, so Magic Git re-checks every few seconds instead. Fix: install fswatch (macOS hosts) or inotifywait (Linux hosts) — see Tool Health — then reconnect.
Nothing refreshes
Symptom: the dot is grey and Change watcher shows Stopped. Cause: nothing is watching this repository. Fix: press ⌘R to refresh by hand (the Dashboard says "changes refresh manually").
Status is slow on a large repository

Turn on git fsmonitor for the repository: Enable filesystem monitor when adding it, or the fsmonitor toggle on its Connections Manager row. It is unavailable for a scoped (dotfiles) repository, which watches only tracked files instead.

topics.title: Access and Credentials
topics.summary: macOS folder-access prompts, and where saved credentials are stored.

sections.text: Grant access prompts

items: Grant access to this worktree — a worktree outside the main repository folder must be selected once before macOS lets Magic Git read it. Choose Folder… and pick it.
Grant access to the main repository — opening a linked worktree needs its main repository, which holds the branches and history. Choose Folder… and pick that repository.
Access is remembered with a security-scoped bookmark, so you are asked only once. SSH repositories never ask.

sections.text: Where saved credentials live

Save connection stores passwords, keys, and tokens in the macOS Keychain on a signed build. An unsigned build cannot reach the Keychain, so it stores them in ~/.config/magic_git/credentials.json, readable only by you (0600). Delete that file to remove them.

sections.title: Plaintext on unsigned builds
sections.text: The credentials.json fallback is protected only by file permissions. Use a signed build for Keychain storage.
